root_cause.text: The software RoCE driver's `rxe_opcode[]` array has zero-filled entries for undefined opcodes, so when an unknown opcode is received, `rxe_opcode[pkt->opcode].length` is zero, causing an integer underflow in `rxe_icrc_hdr()` (length - RXE_BTH_BYTES) that passes a huge value to `rxe_crc32()`, resulting in an out-of-bounds read of the skb payload.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states that `rxe_opcode[]` has 256 entries but is only populated for defined IB opcodes; any other entry (e.g., opcode 0xff) is zero-initialized, so length == 0. The existing check `pkt->paylen < header_size(pkt) + bth_pad(pkt) + RXE_ICRC_SIZE` degenerates to `pkt->paylen < 0 + bth_pad(pkt) + RXE_ICRC_SIZE`, failing to constrain the payload. Later, `rxe_icrc_hdr()` computes `rxe_opcode[pkt->opcode].length - RXE_BTH_BYTES`, underflows, and passes a huge value to `rxe_crc32()`. The patch adds a rejection of packets where `rxe_opcode[pkt->opcode].mask` or `rxe_opcode[pkt->opcode].length` is zero before any length arithmetic.
